# Brief for the coach

## What's in force right now

The program in force is the third version, an amendment adopted on 4 Nov 2026, emphasis hypertrophy, titled "Five compounds around the PT Tuesday". Its stated reason: the engine update removed three cutover workarounds, so the counted pull-up variants now give the pull-up a real weekly set target, and a conditioning session can sit beside a lifting day, so the kettlebell-swing finisher left Monday for its own EMOM session.

It has ten sessions. Both rotation weeks are identical except Tuesday, which alternates the PT's chest-and-back session with the PT's legs-and-core session (both at the gym, both with no lines of their own, estimated at chest 6 / lats 6 / biceps 3 sets and quads 6 / glutes 4 / abs 4 sets respectively).

- **Monday · OHP, back and arms** (75-minute cap): Overhead Press warm-ups 1×5 and 1×3, then a top set 1×5 at RPE 8 and 4×6 back-offs at 85 % of the top, 180 s rest; Chest Supported Row (Dumbbell) 4×8–12 RPE 8, 120 s; Lateral Raise 3×12–15 RPE 8 and Rear Delt Fly 3×12–15 RPE 8 supersetted, 60 s. Kettlebell swings now run alongside as a separate 12-minute EMOM, 12 swings a minute at RPE 7, 40 lb bell.
- **Wednesday · Pull-up volume and core** (75): Scapular Pull Up 2×6–8 activation at RPE 5; Negative Pull Up 3×2–4 RPE 8; Pull Up (Band) 4×5–8 RPE 8; Flexed Arm Hang 2×20 s; Lying Leg Raise 3×10–15 RPE 8 supersetted with Suitcase Carry 4×30 s; Single Leg Standing Calf Raise 3×10–15 RPE 8.
- **Friday · Strict pull-up test, squat and legs** (75): one strict pull-up test rep at RPE 10; Back Squat warm-ups 1×5, 1×3, 1×2, top set 1×5 RPE 8, 4×5 back-offs at 85 %; Romanian Deadlift 3×6–10 RPE 8; Split Squat (Dumbbell) 3×8–12 RPE 8; Shoulder Press (Dumbbell) 3×8–12 RPE 8; Single Leg Standing Calf Raise 3×10–15 RPE 8; Ab Wheel Rollout 3×6–12 RPE 8.
- **Saturday · Bench, back and arms** (90): Bench Press warm-ups 1×8, 1×5, 1×3, top set 1×5 RPE 8, 4×6 back-offs; Bent Over Row 4×6–10 RPE 8; Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell) 3×8–12 RPE 8; Dip Negatives 3×3–5 RPE 8; Overhead Triceps Extension 3×10–15 RPE 8; Lateral Raise 3×12–15 RPE 8.
- **Sunday · Deadlift and legs** (90): Deadlift warm-ups 1×5, 1×3, top set 1×5 RPE 8, 3×5 back-offs; Bulgarian Split Squat 3×8–12 RPE 8; Hip Thrust 3×8–12 RPE 8; Pull Up (Band) 3×5–8 RPE 8; Bicep Curl (Dumbbell) 3×8–12 RPE 8; Hammer Curl 3×10–12 RPE 8; Farmers Walk 3×30 s, starting at 50 lb.
- Optional: the swing EMOM (12 minutes, cap 16, stepping 2 minutes at a time, 12 reps per minute up to 15); the strength circuit (4 rounds, cap 6, 16-minute cap, goblet squat 10 / ring push-up 12 / swing 12 at 40 lb / mountain climber 16, RPE 8); and a daily dead hang, 2×20 s at RPE 5.

Weekly set targets in this version: 10 hard sets per muscle; bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, back squat 5; pull-up 10 counting negatives and banded reps. Deload: after at most 6 hard weeks, cut sets 40 %, loads 0 %, cap RPE at 8, and test the priority lifts.

The progress report has nothing to show yet: the set-by-muscle tables are empty because the block only opened on 1 Nov and no week has closed.

## Why the biceps question came up

In this program all direct biceps work is on Sunday: Bicep Curl 3×8–12 and Hammer Curl 3×10–12, six sets in one session, plus whatever the PT does on chest-and-back Tuesdays (estimated 3 biceps sets). The old program, for comparison, spread curls out: incline curls on Saturday pull (week A) and Monday pull (week B), bicep curls on Sunday, hammer curls on Saturday and Sunday. Joe's profile says direct biceps work should be dumbbell curls, not barbell.

Joe's profile also records: born 18 Jun 1989, 172 cm, intermediate lifter, body fat about 25–27 %, maintenance phase now with a later small deficit of about 0.3 % of bodyweight a week, protein aim 175 g a day. Long-term targets: five strict pull-ups, bench 1.25×BW, OHP 0.75×BW, deadlift 2×BW, squat 1.5×BW. Home bar tops out at 228 lb; squat or deadlift moves to the gym when a top set reaches about 220 lb. Sleep has been the limiter since August. Nothing limiting as of 1 Nov 2026.

## The proposed change

I prepared a draft that adds one line to the end of Monday's session: **Incline Curl (Dumbbell), 3 sets of 8–12 reps at RPE 8, 75 seconds rest, double progression** (add load once every set reaches 12). Cues: bench at about 45°, arms hanging straight down behind the torso, elbows stay back with a full stretch at the bottom, no shoulder swing. The reason recorded with it: direct biceps work was six sets in one session; an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap.

The rehearsal (which writes nothing) says adopting it would:

- Record a **fourth program version**, an amendment, starting in rotation week A, **continuing the block that opened on 1 Nov** rather than resetting it.
- Change exactly one thing: Monday gains the incline curl. No sessions added or removed, no other lines touched, no defaults silently filled in.
- Leave the explicit start loads unchanged: Farmers Walk 50 lb (45.36 kg) on Sunday, Kettlebell Swing 40 lb (18.14 kg) in both conditioning sessions. **No start load is set for the incline curl.** The weekly plan will have to derive one from Joe's past incline-curl logs, or you and Joe should pick a weight before the first Monday.
- Estimated session times against caps: Monday 53 of 75 minutes (with the new line), Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90. Nothing is near its cap.
- A Hevy check ran first: nothing new logged between 20:40 and 20:53 UTC on 4 Nov.

**What Joe must agree to:** three extra sets of incline dumbbell curls on Mondays, after the lateral raise / rear delt fly superset, in the 8–12 rep range at an effort of 8 out of 10, progressing by load once all three sets hit 12. That takes Monday from four exercises to five and his direct biceps work from six sets a week to nine over two days. Nothing else about his week changes.

## Warnings from the rehearsal and what they mean

**Three Hevy routines have drifted from the plan approved on 2 Nov 2026.** Someone (Joe, or Hevy itself) has edited set-level details in three routines since the engine last pushed them — not the exercise list, just numbers:

- One routine: the duration on the first exercise's second set.
- Another: reps on the first exercise's fifth, sixth and seventh sets, and the weight on the second exercise's first three sets.
- A third: weights on all four sets of the third exercise, durations on both sets of the fourth, and weights on the first three sets of the sixth.

The output names these only by their internal references, so I can't tell you which sessions they are from this alone. These drifts are not caused by the incline-curl change. They matter because the next push to Hevy would overwrite Joe's hand edits, and because the engine can't be sure what Joe is actually following this week. They clear when the next week plan carries an override matching the edits, or when the next push rewrites the routines. Worth asking Joe what he changed by hand this week and whether he wants those numbers kept.

**Deadlift target is 4 hard sets a week, below the 5–15 band for a maintenance phase.** This is already acknowledged in the program, carried over from the current version, with the reasoning: Sunday plans exactly four hard deadlift sets (the top set and three back-offs), Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern, and the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday, so a target of 5 would fire an under-target flag every week the session is done as written. It stays as a noted judgement call; nothing needs doing.

**The Friday strict pull-up test rep is flagged as a scheme that doesn't match a hypertrophy emphasis** — it's a single all-out test rep at RPE 10 on a held (non-progressing) scheme. The rehearsal output was cut off at that point (about 860 characters unseen), so I can't confirm from this run whether that warning is already acknowledged or whether the fourth version needs an acknowledgement before it will adopt cleanly. The test rep is deliberate per Joe's profile — strict sets become real work once the test rep passes about five — so if it isn't yet acknowledged, the acknowledgement would say exactly that. I'd re-run the rehearsal and read the tail before adopting.

## Where this leaves you

Nothing has been written. The draft with the incline curl sits ready; adopting it records the fourth version as described above. Before that, two things to settle with Joe: a starting weight for the incline curl, and what he changed by hand in Hevy this week so the drift can be resolved rather than overwritten.

first.text:
It's just the label for the fourth version of your program. The one you're training on now is the third, adopted on Tuesday when the swing finisher moved into its own session. Adding the incline curl makes a fourth, and because it's a small amendment rather than a new design, your current block keeps running from where it started on 1 November. Nothing resets.

Two things worth settling before I lock it in:

- **A starting weight.** I didn't set one, so the first Monday would take it from your past incline curl logs. If you'd rather pick, tell me a dumbbell weight you'd hit 8 to 12 clean reps with at an 8 out of 10 and I'll put it in.
- **Your Hevy edits.** Three of your routines have had numbers changed by hand this week (a hold time, some reps, some weights). Those aren't from this change, but the next time I push the plan to Hevy they'd be overwritten. If you tell me what you changed and want kept, I'll carry it into next week's plan.

Neither blocks the curl. Say yes and I'll adopt it as described, or give me the weight first.
